Reviewer4's independent disposable reproduction job c28e84c6c0f04b51a2ff4f04cf0636c0 at exact SHA (diagnostic exit 0) reports claim Claimed -> start StartAuthorized -> cached Dispatching -> VerifiedNoSend -> project Released -> fake account FakeAccountReleased -> provider.send(stale, effect, ackLost) returns Unknown, durable acceptedCount=1; independent invariant rejects FalseNoSendDurableProvider only after the false release. Ordinary frozen checks were 17/17 Node and 9/9 .NET model-only; these do not refute the counterexample. I independently established source plausibility, not a second physical reproduction; terminal job outcome is reviewer-recorded.
SCOPE: Directly within original Phase A obligation: no send from stale/untrusted proof, no false no-send or completion/release, unknown effect retains account reservation, independent provider/account evidence and multi-client replay/restart. Not a new production threat model. Prior 10877 authorized durable external fake-provider receipt and generated post-send histories, but this later discovered distinct stale-authorization ordering remained untested.
IMPACT: A stale Dispatching handle can produce an accepted fake provider effect AFTER a no-send proof and after project/account release, while project truth still says completed/no send. In the fixture the resulting independent invariant failure is real; the current green tests are insufficient for Phase A safety. Real-world analogue requires a late sender allowed to use stale authority and a provider lacking an atomic fence; neither production StageB nor a live browser/provider/account was tested. No production defect or exploit established.
PRACTICALITY / ALTERNATIVES: NARROW to smallest sound Phase A remedy within original seven files only (scripts/tests/scheduler-property-project-effect-20261122/** and docs/testing/scheduler-property-project-effect-20261122.md): exercise seeded cached Dispatching snapshot across no-send, project release, fake-account release, restart and late attempted send; check independent provider acceptedCount, project/account disposition and invariants; include a mutation that permits late send and goes RED. Correct fake-provider/reference semantics so no-session proof is prospective (all previously issued dispatch rights demonstrably quiesced/revoked) rather than merely no receipt at observation. A minimal disposable provider-owned atomic seal/fence or equivalent verified quiescence before no-send proof is one possibility, not a prescribed API. Prove both send-wins (no-send/release denied, reservation kept) and seal-wins (late stale send denied, zero accepted) schedules. If the existing seam cannot model that safety, fail closed/mark true no-send unsupported instead of passing static absent-session proof. Do not require exhaustive real concurrency, a new cross-ledger production protocol, shared fsproj, StageB native changes or broader architecture changes. Add targeted docs with exact limitations; obtain fresh independent immutable review of corrected test/docs SHA.
SECURITY RESIDUAL: Fake file-backed boundary and single-process/sequential interleavings are not a production provider authorization guarantee; real in-flight calls, crash recovery, cross-store atomicity, browser sends and F# B1/B2 end-to-end remain unverified. Old StageB negative control cannot be promoted by this result. Separate release/cutover approval is required. Corrective Work is AUTHORIZED ONLY as scoped continuation of existing original Phase A task; no new task/review-of-adjudication created. No code edits, no live sends, main push, deploy, migration or schedules. This is terminal and one-pass.
